findings.problem: The diff removes id="settings-form" from the instances form (line 134) and the form="settings-form" attributes from the General fields. It moves those fields into a separate <form> (lines 18-90). That form's only submit button is the 'Save Settings' button at about line 241, and it belongs to the instances form, so the General values are never posted. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:529-540) builds the whole `general` block from form.get(...) with fallback defaults: safe_log_level(None), hard_max_per_cycle=0, max_history_rows=1000, request_timeout=30, page_size=50, tracking_window_minutes=60, max_consecutive_failures=5. It also sets skip_unreleased to `form.get('skip_unreleased') == 'on'`, which becomes False. Every 'Save Settings' click therefore overwrites the user's General config on disk with these defaults. This re-introduces the exact bug that HEAD commit 542d5dd fixed.
findings.title: Saving Settings resets every General setting to its default
findings.why_it_matters: Silent config data loss: a user who edits only a Radarr/Sonarr instance has log level, caps, timeouts and skip_unreleased reset without being told.

findings.fix_hint: associate the General fields with the main settings form via form="settings-form" instead of a separate button-less form
findings.problem: The new <form> at lines 18-90 wraps only the General fields and contains no submit button (the template's only submit buttons are at about lines 109, 232 and 241, all in other forms). The form has several number inputs, so pressing Enter does not submit it either: HTML only submits on Enter without a submit button when the form has a single text-like field. Changes to log level, caps, timeouts, tracking window or skip_unreleased cannot reach save_settings.
findings.title: General settings form has no submit control, so General edits can never be saved
findings.why_it_matters: The General settings section looks editable, but nothing the user changes there is ever saved.

CSRF protection exists globally (`OriginCheckMiddleware`) and is unaffected by this diff. This is a pure template-structure change (Jinja2/HTML), and I traced the full behavioral path through `triggarr/web/routes.py::save_settings`. No injection, XSS, secrets, auth, data-exposure, path-traversal, SSRF, deserialization, or mass-assignment issue is introduced by this diff — all interpolated values (`{{ log_level }}`, `{{ hard_max_per_cycle }}`, etc.) were already present pre-diff and remain Jinja2-autoescaped; no new sinks were added.

I did trace one real, demonstrated behavioral regression that falls outside the required security categories, so I'm reporting it only as a note rather than forcing it into a miscategorized finding: splitting the General-settings fields into their own `<form>` (no longer linked via `form="settings-form"`) means the per-app "Save Settings" button — the only reachable submit button post-diff, since the new General `<form>` has no submit button and contains multiple number/select fields, which per the HTML spec blocks implicit Enter-key submission — now posts without any General fields. In `triggarr/web/routes.py:530-540`, `save_settings` rebuilds the `general` config block from `form.get(...)` on every POST with no "preserve existing value if absent" fallback (unlike the per-app instance branch at lines 581-594, which does preserve). So every legitimate instance edit/add now silently resets `log_level`, `hard_max_per_cycle`, `max_history_rows`, `request_timeout`, `page_size`, `tracking_window_minutes`, `max_consecutive_failures`, and `skip_unreleased` to hardcoded defaults. This is not attacker-exploitable (anyone who can POST to `/settings` could already set arbitrary values directly, with or without this template), so it's a correctness/data-integrity bug, not a security vulnerability — flagging for the bugs/correctness reviewer rather than as a security finding.
